newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar weakens, May holds above support.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar weakens, May holds above support.

text.p: London's spot May white sugar contract marched briskly lower in light activity on Wednesday morning but should hold above chart support at $303 a tonne, traders said.
Early trade and broker selling forced May down to a low of $304.00 and while position gently climbed higher it only retained a slight premium to the second-month August contract.
"We saw some very good selling earlier on which pushed the market down and the May/August has come in," said one trader. "But May on its own is going to find support around the $303 area."
At 1240 GMT May was down $1.60 at $304.50 and August down $1.50 at $304.20. Volume was dominated by May and amounted to a light 460 lots.
Traders continued to monitor the nearby May/August as the spot position moved lower in a correction to last week's rally. August/October narrowed by about $1.00.
May/August was trading at even money and while offers were noted at 50 cents over, the spread is expected to narrow further into a discount.
"It'll probably come into a discount situation as there is a bit of buying at around 50 (cents) under," the trader said.
In physical news, European traders said Iraq had postponed its tender to buy sugar under the U.N. oil-for-food deal until February 28.
But the quantity of sugar required by Iraq is still unclear, with traders mentioning total amounts ranging between 25,000 and 120,000 tonnes.
Syria tenders on Wednesday to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws, both amounts for April shipment. Results are to be made known on Thursday.
The Paris market also moved lower but volume was much smaller than in London at just 90 lots.
May and August were both down $1.30, at $304.00 and $303.80 respectively.
